openings.claim: A removable registration joint may resist sliding without making seal compression the main lateral load path. The nearest rival is increased corner pressure relying on seal friction; the supplied opposite-corner lift challenges that rival.
openings.delta: Use the four strips as two paired, rubber-padded rim shoes, drilled only in the strips. Four bolts clamp the shoes to an accessible rim underside; the remaining two provide adjustable hatch-edge stops. Route the fabric straps from the shoes to bias the hatch toward two orthogonal stops and retain it vertically. Use cord for recoverable connected assemblies. Shoe placement and strap routing must permit complete removal from the marked opening.
openings.prediction: If the shoes hold and straps reach, hatch position follows the stops rather than stronger corner compression: after ten opening cycles, displacement remains within 1 mm under the supplied 20 N pull, including the final right-contact card disturbance. Reopening takes at most 30 seconds, with no new visible seal tears. This is unverified.
openings.probe: First measure rim purchase, strap reach, stop contact and cord routing with the ruler. Abandon fabrication if these cannot work within supplied stock. Within ninety minutes, build one configuration. Use ten numbered opening/closure/pull trials in twenty minutes; place the 1 mm card at the marked right contact on trial ten. Record position before/under pull, corner lift, reopening time and visible seal condition. Compare the displacement and lift pattern with supplied untreated sliding and pressure-induced lift. Shoe motion, absent stop contact, displacement above 1 mm, reopening above 30 seconds, obstruction or a new tear defeats this configuration; do not deploy it on a stop cap alone.
assumptions: Accessible rim underside and sufficient strip overlap are unknown.
Straps can reach and be secured using supplied parts; two stops and strap bias can constrain the actual sideways-pull direction.
Padding and moderate shoe tightening avoid permanent deformation; clearance tolerates the disturbed closure without relying on extra corner pressure.
Ten cycles and measurements fit twenty minutes; cord keeps assemblies recoverable outside the opening.

assessment: One uncertain probe opening. Missing rim geometry and attachment capacity prevent a feasibility or performance claim. No relaxation of hard constraints is proposed.
